title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
abstract: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $π$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP size, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of smaller $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of larger $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific intervals ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the structural localization of active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.
summary: This work applies TAO-DFT to study ladder-type phenylenes, revealing that their electronic properties are not monotonic but exhibit a distinct damped periodic oscillation with a period of three. This periodicity dictates a transition between closed-shell and polyradical states, offering fundamental guidelines for the rational design of these carbon-based nanomaterials.
main_problem: Accurately predicting the electronic properties of extended pi-conjugated systems containing radical character, which is a major theoretical challenge due to strong static correlation effects.
main_result: The electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes exhibit a unique damped periodic oscillation, with highly correlated hotspots appearing at intervals $n = 3k - 1$. This periodicity governs the transition from nonradical to polyradical character.
method: The study employs Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory (TAO-DFT) to efficiently capture static correlation effects in these large systems.
model_or_system: The physical system is ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), which are extended $\pi$-conjugated systems formed by $n$ fused four-membered carbon rings, studied for $n=1$ to $40$.
key_observables: Singlet-Triplet Energy Gap (EST), radical character, Symmetrized von Neumann Entropy (SvN), Vertical Ionization Potential ($I_v$), Electron Affinity ($E_a$), and Fundamental Gap ($E_g$).
important_parameters: The periodicity of 3 in the electronic structure, and the specific structural localization of active orbitals along the central ladder framework.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of TAO-DFT, which is assumed to accurately model static correlation effects, overcoming limitations of standard KS-DFT.
figures_summary: Figures systematically present calculated properties (gap, IP, EA, etc.) and real-space orbital distributions for small $n$ (up to $n=5$), demonstrating the evolution of electronic structure.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the electronic structure evolution of $n$-LPs using TAO-DFT, focusing on how key observables like the S-T gap and radical character oscillate with chain length $n$, contrasting this periodicity with monotonic trends seen in other nanographenes.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, quantitative understanding of how structural periodicity dictates electronic correlation in extended $\pi$-systems, which is crucial for designing next-generation organic electronic materials.
